original_question: Study the complexity function of polygonal symplectic billiards, where the complexity p(n) counts the number of length-n subwords arising from symbolic codings of billiard trajectories by polygon sides.
target_in_paper: Serge Tabachnikov, subsection Complexity of polygonal symplectic billiards: Problem: study the complexity of polygonal symplectic billiards. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right open problem and the right notion of complexity: coding symplectic billiard trajectories by polygon sides and counting distinct length-n subwords arising from those codes. That is exactly the setup given immediately before the problem statement in arXiv:2602.12896. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))
missing_details: The paper’s complexity is formed from the collection of bi-infinite symbolic words coming from all billiard trajectories, not from a single orbit or a preselected subsystem. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))

To make the question stand alone, one should specify the single-polygon planar setting and, following the foundational paper cited nearby, the convex-polygon model used there. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))

One should say that only trajectories for which the symplectic billiard map is defined are coded; in the polygonal model the map is not defined when an iterate hits a vertex, and in the single-polygon convex setting it is also excluded when the tail and head lie on parallel sides. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1912.09404))

The paper does not state a conjectured asymptotic law such as polynomial, cubic, or subexponential growth for polygonal symplectic billiards; those growth facts are mentioned only for conventional and outer billiards as motivation. A paper-faithful reformulation should therefore ask to determine the growth of p(n), not presuppose a regime. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))

The note that some polygonal symplectic billiards have all trajectories periodic, so the complexity can have zero growth rate, is part of the intended scope and should be retained in the sharpened question. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))
refined_question: Let P be a planar convex polygon, with its sides labeled by a finite alphabet, and consider all symplectic billiard trajectories in P for which the polygonal symplectic billiard map is defined. For each such trajectory, record the bi-infinite symbolic word of the labels of the sides visited by the trajectory, and let p_P(n) be the number of distinct length-n subwords occurring among all these bi-infinite codes. Determine the asymptotic growth of the complexity function p_P(n) for polygonal symplectic billiards, allowing in particular for the fully periodic examples noted in the paper, where the complexity may have zero growth rate. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper. The exact target in arXiv:2602.12896 is not a conjecture with a prescribed bound but a short open problem in Serge Tabachnikov’s section: after defining side-label symbolic coding and the associated complexity function, the paper simply asks to study the complexity of polygonal symplectic billiards. The extra sharpening needed for a stand-alone version is therefore mostly contextual: make explicit that the words are bi-infinite codes of all admissible trajectories, and import from the cited foundational single-polygon paper the nearby hidden scope that this is the planar convex-polygon symplectic billiard model. It is also important not to overstate the question into a claim about polynomial or cubic growth, because the paper does not conjecture that; instead it only gives those facts for conventional and outer billiards as background. Finally, the paper explicitly warns that fully periodic examples exist, so the refined question should not build in any assumption of positive or nonzero growth. No ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree restriction, or nilpotency condition appears here; this is a symbolic-dynamical growth problem, not an algebraic one. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))
